newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE-100 seen testing all-time highs.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE-100 seen testing all-time highs.

text.p: UK's FTSE 100 index could test its all-time closing high by the time of the next week's election, despite failing to make a significant break through the 4,400 level in recent sessions, chart analysts said on Friday.

"The FTSE chart looks basically healthy but the market is becalmed because of the election," said Chris Chaitow, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities. The FTSE 100 index fell 4.1 points to 4,384.4 by 0852 GMT.
"Breaking through 4,310 was the key at the beginning of the week," Chaitow said.
"I can see the chart making a run at 4,444 (its all-time closing high) around the time of the election and possibly another 100 points thereafter, mainly beacause of the relief factor," said Chaitow.
However Chaitow said with the Dow finishing weaker overnight and European markets opening mixed, the FTSE 100 index lacked upward momentum in the short-term.
Weak gilts and U.S. Treasury bonds were also weighing on shares, said Susan Rigg at Chart Analysis.
"The weakness of gilts and of U.S. Treasuries means there is a lack of follow through," Rigg said.
LIFFE's long gilt future fell a 1/4 of a point in early trading.
